Explicitly NOT authorised without a new decision: networking or topology changes, PMS configuration or traffic, financial behaviour, database schema, security or architecture boundaries, and Go-Live.

guest_path_as_found.addressing: Kea serving 192.168.77.100-200 on br-g-00d1fa1a with option 114 pointing at http://192.168.77.1:8380/. Live leases present; nine devices on the bridge.
guest_path_as_found.dns: Unbound answering on the guest gateway.
guest_path_as_found.portal: portald serving on :8380; the page offers all six sign-in methods -- voucher, personal account, email OTP, room number, post-stay PIN and phone OTP.
guest_path_as_found.pms_mirror: CONNECTED / CONTINUOUS / IN_SYNC, 468 in-house stays, every one carrying a room number and a reservation id.
guest_path_as_found.captive_detection: Working. Operating-system and application probes are intercepted and answered with the portal, observed in portald's own log.
guest_path_as_found.conversion: NO guest has attempted a sign-in for nine days; the last successful session was 2026-09-12. The current guest traffic is captive probes from operating systems and apps, not people. The pilot is available but is not being exercised.

defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: The dashboard reported 'No address range is configured, so this appliance cannot hand out addresses here' for the guest network Kea was actively serving 101 addresses from, and had been doing so throughout the pilot.
defect_found_and_fixed.root_cause: The dashboard's pool-size query guarded with network(p.start_ip::cidr) = network(p.end_ip::cidr). An inet host cast to cidr carries a /32, so that compares 192.168.77.100/32 with 192.168.77.200/32 and is true only when a pool is a single address. Every real range failed it, the sum returned NULL, and COALESCE turned 'I excluded everything' into a confident zero.
defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_matters_in_a_pilot: The screen does not say unknown; it states that the appliance cannot hand out addresses. That sends an operator to repair a working DHCP configuration, and it makes a real addressing outage indistinguishable from the normal display.
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: The guard now asks the question the arithmetic assumes -- that start and end lie in the same /24, because the size is computed from the fourth octet -- and a reversed range is rejected rather than subtracting from the total. Verified against the appliance's database: the pool that scored 0 scores 101, and a range spanning two /24s is still correctly excluded.
defect_found_and_fixed.scope: One read-only reporting query in edged. No DHCP, Kea, netd, nftables, schema or guest-network configuration was touched.

checked_and_left_alone.devices_online: The same card shows 'Devices online 0' while nine devices sit on the bridge. That figure counts SIGNED-IN sessions, of which there are none, so it is accurate. It was checked rather than assumed.

product_owner_decision_requested.what: nftables DNATs unauthenticated guest traffic on port 443 to 192.168.77.1:8343, and nothing listens there. portald logs 'portald HTTPS disabled - cert missing' at every start, because /etc/stayconnect/tls/ does not exist on the appliance at all.
product_owner_decision_requested.consequence: A guest who opens an HTTPS site before signing in gets a connection refused rather than the portal. The HTTP captive path is unaffected and is what device captive-detection uses, which is why the portal still appears normally -- observed working during this assessment.
product_owner_decision_requested.why_it_is_not_decided_here: It is not a regression. SYSTEM_OVERVIEW documents the listener as conditional -- 'HTTPS only if cert exists' -- netd's own portal_listen health check asserts the HTTP port only, and no portal-certificate tooling has ever existed in the repository. Both available remedies fall outside this mission's authorisation: minting a portal certificate is PKI and a security-boundary decision, and it buys a certificate warning in place of a connection error because a captive portal necessarily presents a certificate for somebody else's domain; removing the port-443 DNAT is a networking change.
product_owner_decision_requested.options: (a) leave it and record the HTTPS captive path as deliberately unserved; (b) authorise a portal certificate and the provisioning for it; or (c) authorise removing the 443 DNAT so the failure is immediate and intentional rather than a redirect to a closed port.

verification.tests: Go build, vet and the edged suite clean. A new test reads the QUERY rather than the prose around it, because the comment explaining the defect quotes the broken predicate; mutation-proven by reintroducing the /32 guard, which fails it.
verification.ci_limitation_recorded: The repository's integration tests are compiled by CI but never executed by it -- the workflows vet '-tags integration' and nothing runs them. A behavioural test behind that tag would look like protection and provide none, so the behaviour was verified directly against the appliance instead.
